chunks: Ali, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Purify your children on the seventh day, for it is more fragrant, purer, and faster for the growth of the flesh, and indeed the earth becomes impure from the urine of the uncircumcised for forty mornings.'

key_terms.طَهِّرُوا: Purify (imperative verb, referring to ritual cleansing or circumcision)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the impurity of an uncircumcised child's urine and the recommended time for purification?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the Sunnah of circumcising children on the seventh day, framing it as a means of physical hygiene and spiritual purity. It further clarifies the jurisprudential ruling that the urine of the uncircumcised (al-aghlaf) renders the earth impure for forty mornings, a duration derived from the time required for the prepuce to heal and the area to dry. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on combining ritual cleanliness (taharah) with practical health benefits in the upbringing of children.
